Q: Why does a call to `ref` on a reference to `substr` produce "LVALUE"? A:

With \substr(...) you did take a reference to a modifiable memory location, since substr() is an lvalue-function, and your $lv prints LVALUE(memory-location). The LVALUE is a special type of reference so ref (and Scalar::Util::reftype) return that label. The memory location contains what substr(...) (would have) returned.

When you print $$lv you get what your substr() call returned, and if you assign to $$lv the original string's corresponding range of characters is changed (since substr is a function that can be used as lvalue).

A command-line program ("one-liner") as an example:

perl -wE'$s = "hello"; $lv = \substr($s, 1, 2); say $lv; say $$lv; 
         $$lv = "WHOA"; say $s'

(I split it into two lines for eaiser reading. In Bash one can still just copy-paste into terminal)

It prints

LVALUE(0x55d494b604d8)
el
hWHOAlo

Once we have that LVALUE reference in $lv we can continue using it -- further writes to $$lv change the original string

perl -wE'$s = "hello"; $lv = \substr($s, 1, 2); 
         for (qw(WHOA A OHYES)) { $$lv = $_; say $s }'

Prints

hWHOAlo
hAlo
hOHYESlo

Q: "Failed to open QEMU pipe 'qemud:network': Invalid argument" error when trying to run app on android emulator A:

This error could be due to two reasons :

  1. Either due to your android emulator / device version.
  2. Due to some error in your java or xml file.

First, change your current minSdkVersion to some other version preferably below 23. Then check your logcat whether it gives some error in your code. Most probably that could be an import error.

In my case, I changed my minSdkVersion from 26 to 17. And it worked for me. Hopefully, it works for you as well.

Q: Arduino and Nextion display with decimal numbers A:

You can use the Xfloat widget and send the value in the same way as number, but you need to change the parameters "vvs0" and "vvs1" on nextion editor, so the widget adjust the value. For example if you wanna show the value 2.53, multiply it by 100 and then set the parameter "vvs0" to 1 and "vvs1" to 2.

Q: Persisting Spark Streaming output A:

I think the small file problem could be resolved somewhat. You may be getting large number of files based on kafka partitions. For me, I have 12 partition Kafka topic and I write using spark.write.mode("append").parquet("/location/on/hdfs").

Now depending on your requirements, you can either add coalesce(1) or more to reduce number of files. Also another option is to increase the micro batch duration. For example, if you can accept 5 minutes delay in writing day, you can have micro batch of 300 seconds.

For the second issues, the batches queue up only because you don't have back pressure enabled. First you should verify what is the max you can process in a single batch. Once you can get around that number, you can set spark.streaming.kafka.maxRatePerPartition value and spark.streaming.backpressure.enabled=true to enable limited number of records per micro batch. If you still cannot meet the demand, then the only options are to either increase partitions on topic or to increase resources on spark application.

Q: VBA and Pivot Tables: getting two data fields A:

I made some revisions to your code so try this:

Sub CreatePivot()
' Create the 5 summary pivot tables using the TRADE_LIST sheet as data
Dim LastRow, LastCol As Long
Dim dataSource, destination As String
Dim wb As Workbook
Dim data_sheet, pivot1 As Worksheet

Set wb = ThisWorkbook
Set data_sheet = wb.Sheets("DATA") 'in your code, you forgot to include WB
Set pivot1 = wb.Sheets("PIVOT")

' (1) Source data from the TRADE_LIST sheet and create a pivot cache from source data _
  to use for each pivot table

'i changed this part to cover all data 
LastRow = data_sheet.Cells(data_sheet.Rows.Count, 1).End(xlUp).Row
LastCol = data_sheet.Cells(1, data_sheet.Columns.Count).End(xlToLeft).Column

'PivotCache creation requires arguments in string format, no need to use Set
dataSource = data_sheet.Name & "!" & data_sheet.Cells(1, 1).Resize(LastRow, LastCol).Address(ReferenceStyle:=xlR1C1)
destination = pivot1.Name & "!" & pivot1.Range("A1").Address(ReferenceStyle:=xlR1C1)

'here we use the datasource and destination
wb.PivotCaches.Create(SourceType:=xlDatabase, SourceData:= _
    dataSource, Version:=xlPivotTableVersion12).CreatePivotTable _
    TableDestination:=destination, TableName:="PivotTable1", DefaultVersion _
    :=xlPivotTableVersion12

'after creating pivot, add the Row Field
With pivot1.PivotTables("PivotTable1").PivotFields("Comment")
    .Orientation = xlRowField
    .Position = 1
End With

'then add the column fields
With pivot1
    .PivotTables("PivotTable1").AddDataField .PivotTables( _
        "PivotTable1").PivotFields("NOM"), "Sum of NOM", xlSum
    .PivotTables("PivotTable1").AddDataField .PivotTables( _
        "PivotTable1").PivotFields("NOM_MOVE"), "Sum of NOM_MOVE", xlSum
End With

End Sub

Hope this get's you started.

Q: How to pass data via URL parameters to a multi-step form on a different domain that refreshes on load? A:

As I said, maybe they can give you some instructions about how to pass data into their UI page correctly. But their design may not make that achievable really anyway.

I suppose another option is to work with them to implement an extra feature in their site which allows you to send a request containing the data, and they will then have some code which understands that and will pre-populate the form for you. This would be extra custom functionality, so obviously if they agree to do this for you it will cost some money. You will have to decide how important this feature is for you, and whether you would pay extra for it.

Q: How to force a transparent status bar on Samsung in Kotlin Multiplatform A:

Samsung usually does not need special status bar handling.

The main issue is that you are setting system bar settings in two places:

  1. enableEdgeToEdge() in MainActivity

  2. Your custom SystemAppearance() composable

On some devices, especially OEM devices like Samsung, this can cause inconsistent behavior because both pieces of code are trying to control the same window flags/colors.

Use one approach only.

For modern Compose apps, prefer enableEdgeToEdge() and remove most of the manual window code.

Example:

override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
    super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)

    enableEdgeToEdge(
        statusBarStyle = SystemBarStyle.dark(
            scrim = android.graphics.Color.TRANSPARENT
        ),
        navigationBarStyle = SystemBarStyle.light(
            scrim = android.graphics.Color.TRANSPARENT,
            darkScrim = android.graphics.Color.TRANSPARENT
        )
    )

    setContent {
        SongBookTheme {
            App()
        }
    }
}

Then remove this from your composable:

window.statusBarColor = Color.Transparent.toArgb()
window.navigationBarColor = Color.Transparent.toArgb()
WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(window, false)

Also make sure your top-level Compose layout actually draws behind the status bar:

Box(
    modifier = Modifier
        .fillMaxSize()
        .background(MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background)
) {
    // your content
}

“transparent status bar” only looks transparent if your app content/background is drawn behind it. If nothing is drawn behind it, some devices may show black.

**TL;DR: **
Do not mix enableEdgeToEdge() with manual system bar color handling. Use enableEdgeToEdge() once in the Activity, then let your Compose content draw behind the bars.
